data.long_meaning: Deviyan is a name derived from Devi, meaning 'Goddess'. In Hindu mythology, Devi is a collective representation of the divine feminine, symbolizing creation, sustenance, and destruction. The name Deviyan carries the meaning “Goddess, Divine” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Deviyan usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess, divine and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.context: Devi is a central figure in Hinduism and is worshipped in various forms and aspects, including as a mother goddess, a warrior goddess, and a destroyer goddess. The name Deviyan is used as a respectful title for these goddesses.

historical_references.reference: The goddess Devi, also known as Durga, was originally a warrior goddess who was invoked to protect the gods during battles. The name Deviyan is used to refer to this form of the goddess.
historical_references.context: The goddess Durga is described as having ten arms, each holding a weapon, and riding on a lion or tiger. She is often depicted as destroying the demon Mahishasura. The name Deviyan emphasizes her warrior qualities and her role as a protector.
